claim: Follicle rupture, the final step in ovulation, utilizes conserved molecular mechanisms including matrix metalloproteinases (Mmps), steroid signaling, and adrenergic signaling.
source: Follicle rupture, the final step in ovulation, utilizes conserved molecular mechanisms including matrix metalloproteinases (Mmps), steroid signaling, and adrenergic signaling.
evidence: This claim is supported by established scientific knowledge and citations in the broader context of the manuscript.

claim: Hindsight (Hnt) is the first transcription factor regulating follicle's competency for ovulation in Drosophila.
source: Here, we identify a zinc-finger transcription factor Hindsight (Hnt) as the first transcription factor regulating follicle's competency for ovulation in Drosophila.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Hnt is not expressed in immature stage-13 follicle cells but is upregulated in mature stage-14 follicle cells.
source: Hnt is not expressed in immature stage-13 follicle cells but is upregulated in mature stage-14 follicle cells, which is essential for follicle rupture/ovulation.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2 and related text.

claim: Hnt upregulation in stage-14 follicle cells is essential for follicle rupture/ovulation.
source: Hnt is not expressed in immature stage-13 follicle cells but is upregulated in mature stage-14 follicle cells, which is essential for follicle rupture/ovulation.
evidence: This is supported by RNAi depletion experiments showing reduced ovulation when Hnt is depleted (Figures 3-4).

claim: Hnt upregulates Mmp2 expression in posterior follicle cells.
source: Hnt upregulates Mmp2 expression in posterior follicle cells (essential for the breakdown of the follicle wall) and Oamb expression in all follicle cells (the receptor for receiving adrenergic signaling and inducing Mmp2 activation).
evidence: This is supported by Mmp2::GFP expression analysis and RT-PCR data in Figure 6.

claim: Mmp2 is essential for the breakdown of the follicle wall.
source: Hnt upregulates Mmp2 expression in posterior follicle cells (essential for the breakdown of the follicle wall) and Oamb expression in all follicle cells (the receptor for receiving adrenergic signaling and inducing Mmp2 activation).
evidence: This is supported by previous work cited in the manuscript and data showing Mmp2 activity is required for follicle rupture.

claim: Hnt upregulates Oamb expression in all follicle cells.
source: Hnt upregulates Mmp2 expression in posterior follicle cells (essential for the breakdown of the follicle wall) and Oamb expression in all follicle cells (the receptor for receiving adrenergic signaling and inducing Mmp2 activation).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data showing reduced Oamb mRNA in hntRNAi egg chambers (Figure 7A-B).

claim: Oamb is the receptor for receiving adrenergic signaling and inducing Mmp2 activation.
source: Hnt upregulates Mmp2 expression in posterior follicle cells (essential for the breakdown of the follicle wall) and Oamb expression in all follicle cells (the receptor for receiving adrenergic signaling and inducing Mmp2 activation).
evidence: This is supported by previous work cited in the manuscript (Lee et al., 2003; Deady and Sun, 2015).

claim: Hnt's role in regulating Mmp2 and Oamb can be replaced by its human homolog Ras-responsive element-binding protein 1 (RREB-1).
source: Hnt's role in regulating Mmp2 and Oamb can be replaced by its human homolog Ras-responsive element-binding protein 1 (RREB-1).
evidence: This is supported by rescue experiments showing RREB-1 overexpression restores Mmp2 and Oamb expression and follicle rupture in hntRNAi egg chambers (Figure 8).

claim: Hnt/RREB-1 plays conserved role in regulating follicle maturation and competency for ovulation.
source: Our data suggest that Hnt/RREB-1 plays conserved role in regulating follicle maturation and competency for ovulation.
evidence: This is inferred from the functional conservation between Hnt and RREB-1 demonstrated in the rescue experiments.

claim: Several proteolytic systems regulate follicle rupture in vertebrates, including matrix metalloproteinase (Mmp), plasminogen activator/plasmin, and ADAMS-TS.
source: Several proteolytic systems have been found to regulate follicle rupture in vertebrates, including matrix metalloproteinase (Mmp), plasminogen activator/plasmin, and ADAMS-TS (Curry and Smith, 2006; Takahashi et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: A surge of luteinizing hormone (LH) serves as a master regulator to initiate the ovulation event in vertebrates.
source: In addition, a surge of luteinizing hormone (LH) serves as a master regulator to initiate the ovulation event and activates the EGF/EGFR-Ras-MAPK signaling pathway to propagate the ovulatory signal from outer granulosa cells to inner cumulus cells in the preovulatory follicles (Conti et al., 2012; Fan et al., 2009, 2011, 2012; Hsieh et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: LH activates the EGF/EGFR-Ras-MAPK signaling pathway to propagate the ovulatory signal from outer granulosa cells to inner cumulus cells in the preovulatory follicles.
source: In addition, a surge of luteinizing hormone (LH) serves as a master regulator to initiate the ovulation event and activates the EGF/EGFR-Ras-MAPK signaling pathway to propagate the ovulatory signal from outer granulosa cells to inner cumulus cells in the preovulatory follicles (Conti et al., 2012; Fan et al., 2009, 2011, 2012; Hsieh et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Molecular mechanisms coupling the Ras-MAPK pathway to the activation of proteolytic systems for follicle rupture are largely unknown.
source: However, molecular mechanisms coupling the Ras-MAPK pathway to the activation of proteolytic systems for follicle rupture are largely unknown.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Ovulation in Drosophila utilizes conserved molecular mechanisms and involves a follicle rupture process to release mature oocytes from the ovary.
source: Ovulation in Drosophila utilizes conserved molecular mechanisms and involves a follicle rupture process to release mature oocytes from the ovary.
evidence: This is supported by the overall findings of the manuscript and previous work.

claim: Drosophila have two ovaries, connected at their posterior ends by bilateral oviducts.
source: Drosophila have two ovaries, connected at their posterior ends by bilateral oviducts (Figure 1).
evidence: This is a well-established anatomical fact illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: Each ovary contains ~16 ovarioles, where egg chambers are assembled in the germarium at the anterior and develop through 14 characteristic stages toward the posterior end.
source: Each ovary contains ~16 ovarioles, where egg chambers are assembled in the germarium at the anterior and develop through 14 characteristic stages toward the posterior end (Spradling, 1993).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Drosophila oogenesis, supported by citation.

claim: Each egg chamber contains one oocyte and 15 nurse cells surrounded by a layer of somatic follicle cells.
source: Each egg chamber contains one oocyte and 15 nurse cells surrounded by a layer of somatic follicle cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Drosophila egg chamber structure.

claim: In stage-14 egg chambers, all nurse cells are degraded, leaving an oocyte surrounded by follicle cells.
source: In stage-14 egg chambers (also named mature follicles), all nurse cells are degraded, leaving an oocyte surrounded by follicle cells; Matrix metalloproteinase 2 (Mmp2) is upregulated in posterior follicle cells (Figure 1; Deady et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge and citation, as well as Figure 1.

claim: Matrix metalloproteinase 2 (Mmp2) is upregulated in posterior follicle cells of stage-14 egg chambers.
source: In stage-14 egg chambers (also named mature follicles), all nurse cells are degraded, leaving an oocyte surrounded by follicle cells; Matrix metalloproteinase 2 (Mmp2) is upregulated in posterior follicle cells (Figure 1; Deady et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by previous work (Deady et al., 2015) and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: Oamb (octopamine receptor in mushroom body) encodes an α-adrenergic receptor-like G-protein-coupled receptor for octopamine (OA).
source: In addition, Oamb (octopamine receptor in mushroom body), encoding an α-adrenergic receptor-like G-protein-coupled receptor for octopamine (OA), is also upregulated in all follicle cells of stage-14 egg chambers (Lee et al., 2003; Deady and Sun, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Oamb is upregulated in all follicle cells of stage-14 egg chambers.
source: In addition, Oamb (octopamine receptor in mushroom body), encoding an α-adrenergic receptor-like G-protein-coupled receptor for octopamine (OA), is also upregulated in all follicle cells of stage-14 egg chambers (Lee et al., 2003; Deady and Sun, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: OA, released from terminal nerves that innervate ovaries, activates Oamb receptor in stage-14 follicle cells, which induces calcium rise and activates Mmp2.
source: OA, released from terminal nerves that innervate ovaries, activates Oamb receptor in stage-14 follicle cells, which induces calcium rise and activates Mmp2 (Deady and Sun, 2015; Heifetz et al., 2014; Middleton et al., 2006; Monastirioti, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Mmp2 enzymatic activity leads to degradation of posterior follicle cells and release of the encapsulated oocyte (called follicle rupture).
source: Mmp2 enzymatic activity leads to degradation of posterior follicle cells and release of the encapsulated oocyte (called follicle rupture; Figure 1; Deady et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by previous work (Deady et al., 2015) and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: The rest of the follicle cells remain at the end of the ovariole to form a corpus luteum after follicle rupture.
source: The rest of the follicle cells remain at the end of the ovariole to form a corpus luteum (Deady et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Local adrenergic signaling has been suggested to regulate mammalian ovulation but no molecular mechanisms have been illustrated.
source: Local adrenergic signaling has also been suggested to regulate mammalian ovulation but no molecular mechanisms have been illustrated (Kannisto et al., 1985; Schmidt et al., 1985).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Ecdysteroid signaling is activated in stage-14 follicle cells and is essential for Drosophila ovulation.
source: In parallel to progesterone signaling in mammalian ovulation, ecdysteroid signaling is also activated in stage-14 follicle cells and is essential for Drosophila ovulation; ecdysteroid signaling modulates OA/Oamb-induced Mmp2 activation, but does not affect Oamb expression nor Mmp2 expression (Knapp and Sun, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Ecdysteroid signaling modulates OA/Oamb-induced Mmp2 activation, but does not affect Oamb expression nor Mmp2 expression.
source: In parallel to progesterone signaling in mammalian ovulation, ecdysteroid signaling is also activated in stage-14 follicle cells and is essential for Drosophila ovulation; ecdysteroid signaling modulates OA/Oamb-induced Mmp2 activation, but does not affect Oamb expression nor Mmp2 expression (Knapp and Sun, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: It is currently unknown what induces Mmp2 and Oamb expression in stage-14 follicle cells and how these follicles become fully competent for ovulation.
source: Thus, it is currently unknown what induces Mmp2 and Oamb expression in stage-14 follicle cells and how these follicles become fully competent for ovulation.
evidence: This is a statement about the gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: The zinc-finger transcription factor Hindsight (Hnt; encoded by gene pebbled) contains 14 C2H2 zinc-finger domains.
source: The zinc-finger transcription factor Hindsight (Hnt; encoded by gene pebbled) contains 14 C2H2 zinc-finger domains and is homologous to mammalian Ras-responsive element-binding protein 1 (RREB-1).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the structure of Hnt.

claim: Hnt is homologous to mammalian Ras-responsive element-binding protein 1 (RREB-1).
source: The zinc-finger transcription factor Hindsight (Hnt; encoded by gene pebbled) contains 14 C2H2 zinc-finger domains and is homologous to mammalian Ras-responsive element-binding protein 1 (RREB-1).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the evolutionary relationship between Hnt and RREB-1.

claim: Both Hnt and RREB-1 bind to similar DNA sequences.
source: Both Hnt and RREB-1 bind to similar DNA sequences, and human RREB-1 can functionally replace Hnt in attenuating expression of nervy and hnt itself in Drosophila salivary gland (Ming et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Human RREB-1 can functionally replace Hnt in attenuating expression of nervy and hnt itself in Drosophila salivary gland.
source: Both Hnt and RREB-1 bind to similar DNA sequences, and human RREB-1 can functionally replace Hnt in attenuating expression of nervy and hnt itself in Drosophila salivary gland (Ming et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: RREB-1 functions downstream of the Ras-MAPK pathway to either suppress or promote Ras target genes in multiple tissues including colon, thyroid, and pancreatic cancers.
source: RREB-1 functions downstream of the Ras-MAPK pathway to either suppress or promote Ras target genes in multiple tissues including colon, thyroid, and pancreatic cancers (Kent et al., 2010, 2013; Mukhopadhyay et al., 2007; Thiagalingam et al., 1996; Zhang et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Hnt is expressed in a variety of tissues in development and plays multiple developmental roles including control of embryonic germ band retraction.
source: Hnt is expressed in a variety of tissues in development and plays multiple developmental roles including control of embryonic germ band retraction (Yip et al., 1997; Reed et al., 2001), regulation of retinal cell fate and morphogenesis (Pickup et al., 2002; Wilk et al., 2004; Pickup et al., 2009; Oliva and Sierralta, 2010; Oliva et al., 2015), maintenance of tracheal epithelial integrity (Wilk et al., 2000, 2004), and differentiation of spermathecae and intestinal stem cells (Sun and Spradling, 2013; Baechler et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Hnt plays multiple developmental roles including regulation of retinal cell fate and morphogenesis.
source: Hnt is expressed in a variety of tissues in development and plays multiple developmental roles including control of embryonic germ band retraction (Yip et al., 1997; Reed et al., 2001), regulation of retinal cell fate and morphogenesis (Pickup et al., 2002; Wilk et al., 2004; Pickup et al., 2009; Oliva and Sierralta, 2010; Oliva et al., 2015), maintenance of tracheal epithelial integrity (Wilk et al., 2000, 2004), and differentiation of spermathecae and intestinal stem cells (Sun and Spradling, 2013; Baechler et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Hnt plays multiple developmental roles including maintenance of tracheal epithelial integrity.
source: Hnt is expressed in a variety of tissues in development and plays multiple developmental roles including control of embryonic germ band retraction (Yip et al., 1997; Reed et al., 2001), regulation of retinal cell fate and morphogenesis (Pickup et al., 2002; Wilk et al., 2004; Pickup et al., 2009; Oliva and Sierralta, 2010; Oliva et al., 2015), maintenance of tracheal epithelial integrity (Wilk et al., 2000, 2004), and differentiation of spermathecae and intestinal stem cells (Sun and Spradling, 2013; Baechler et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Hnt plays multiple developmental roles including differentiation of spermathecae and intestinal stem cells.
source: Hnt is expressed in a variety of tissues in development and plays multiple developmental roles including control of embryonic germ band retraction (Yip et al., 1997; Reed et al., 2001), regulation of retinal cell fate and morphogenesis (Pickup et al., 2002; Wilk et al., 2004; Pickup et al., 2009; Oliva and Sierralta, 2010; Oliva et al., 2015), maintenance of tracheal epithelial integrity (Wilk et al., 2000, 2004), and differentiation of spermathecae and intestinal stem cells (Sun and Spradling, 2013; Baechler et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Hnt is expressed in follicle cells of stage 7-10A egg chambers, where it functions as a downstream target of Notch signaling to suppress Hedgehog signaling and to induce the mitotic/endocycle transition.
source: Hnt is also expressed in follicle cells of stage 7-10A egg chambers, where it functions as a downstream target of Notch signaling to suppress Hedgehog signaling and to induce the mitotic/endocycle transition (Sun and Deng, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Hnt continues its expression in anterior follicle cells throughout late oogenesis.
source: Hnt continues its expression in anterior follicle cells throughout late oogenesis.
evidence: This is an observation from the study.

claim: Hnt expression in mainbody follicle cells is downregulated from stage 10B to stage 13 and re-upregulated in stage-14.
source: In contrast, Hnt expression in mainbody follicle cells is downregulated from stage 10B to stage 13 and re-upregulated in stage-14 (Deady et al., 2015), where its role is unknown.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Few downstream targets of Hnt have been identified.
source: Moreover, few downstream targets of Hnt have been identified and its relationship to Ras signaling is also unknown.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Hnt's relationship to Ras signaling is unknown.
source: Moreover, few downstream targets of Hnt have been identified and its relationship to Ras signaling is also unknown.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Hnt expression in stage-14 follicle cells is essential for follicle rupture partly by upregulation of Oamb and Mmp2 expression in these follicle cells.
source: By using molecular and genetic tools, we demonstrated that Hnt expression in stage-14 follicle cells is essential for follicle rupture partly by upregulation of Oamb and Mmp2 expression in these follicle cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data in Figures 6-7.

claim: Hnt functions as an essential transcription factor to prime follicles to be competent for follicle rupture/ovulation.
source: Thus, Hnt functions as an essential transcription factor to prime follicles to be competent for follicle rupture/ovulation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: There are three distinct patterns of Hnt expression throughout stage-14 egg chambers.
source: Upon closer examination, we found three distinct patterns of Hnt expression throughout stage-14 egg chambers: (I) high Hnt expression in anterior and posterior but low/no Hnt in the middle follicle cells ('A/P-Hnt' egg chambers; Figure 2A and F, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B); (II) high Hnt expression in all follicle cells ('high-Hnt' egg chambers; Figure 2B and G); (III) low Hnt expression in all follicle cells ('low-Hnt' egg chambers; Figure 2C and H; also see Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2.

claim: 86% of A/P-Hnt egg chambers had medium-level GFP expression driven by FC1.
source: 86% of A/P-Hnt egg chambers had medium-level GFP expression driven by FC1, while more than 73% of high-Hnt and 80% of low-Hnt egg chambers had high-level GFP expression (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: This is quantitative data from the study shown in Figure 2D.

claim: More than 73% of high-Hnt egg chambers had high-level GFP expression driven by FC1.
source: 86% of A/P-Hnt egg chambers had medium-level GFP expression driven by FC1, while more than 73% of high-Hnt and 80% of low-Hnt egg chambers had high-level GFP expression (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: This is quantitative data from the study shown in Figure 2D.

claim: 80% of low-Hnt egg chambers had high-level GFP expression driven by FC1.
source: 86% of A/P-Hnt egg chambers had medium-level GFP expression driven by FC1, while more than 73% of high-Hnt and 80% of low-Hnt egg chambers had high-level GFP expression (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: This is quantitative data from the study shown in Figure 2D.

claim: A/P-Hnt egg chambers are the youngest stage-14 egg chambers.
source: This indicates that A/P-Hnt egg chambers are the youngest, which is consistent with the observation that A/P-Hnt egg chambers typically have more residual nurse-cell nuclei than the other two types of egg chambers (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is inferred from FC1 expression levels and nurse cell nuclei counts shown in Figure 2.

claim: A/P-Hnt egg chambers typically have more residual nurse-cell nuclei than high-Hnt and low-Hnt egg chambers.
source: This indicates that A/P-Hnt egg chambers are the youngest, which is consistent with the observation that A/P-Hnt egg chambers typically have more residual nurse-cell nuclei than the other two types of egg chambers (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is quantitative data from the study shown in Figure 2E.

claim: High-Hnt egg chambers still contained one or two nurse-cell nuclei.
source: In addition, high-Hnt egg chambers still contained one or two nurse-cell nuclei, while low-Hnt egg chambers typically did not contain nurse-cell nuclei and were skinner and dehydrated (Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is observational data from the study shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Low-Hnt egg chambers typically did not contain nurse-cell nuclei and were skinner and dehydrated.
source: In addition, high-Hnt egg chambers still contained one or two nurse-cell nuclei, while low-Hnt egg chambers typically did not contain nurse-cell nuclei and were skinner and dehydrated (Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is observational data from the study shown in Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Nurse-cell nuclei are progressively degraded starting around stage-12 by a non-cell-autonomous mechanism to generate fully matured egg chambers.
source: Because nurse-cell nuclei are progressively degraded starting around stage-12 by a non-cell-autonomous mechanism to generate fully matured egg chambers, which have no nurse cell nuclei and are dehydrated (Drummond-Barbosa and Spradling, 2004; Timmons et al., 2016), the above analysis demonstrates that high-Hnt egg chambers are at the intermediate stage, while low-Hnt egg chambers are the most mature egg chambers.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Fully matured egg chambers have no nurse cell nuclei and are dehydrated.
source: Because nurse-cell nuclei are progressively degraded starting around stage-12 by a non-cell-autonomous mechanism to generate fully matured egg chambers, which have no nurse cell nuclei and are dehydrated (Drummond-Barbosa and Spradling, 2004; Timmons et al., 2016), the above analysis demonstrates that high-Hnt egg chambers are at the intermediate stage, while low-Hnt egg chambers are the most mature egg chambers.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: High-Hnt egg chambers are at the intermediate stage of stage-14 development.
source: Because nurse-cell nuclei are progressively degraded starting around stage-12 by a non-cell-autonomous mechanism to generate fully matured egg chambers, which have no nurse cell nuclei and are dehydrated (Drummond-Barbosa and Spradling, 2004; Timmons et al., 2016), the above analysis demonstrates that high-Hnt egg chambers are at the intermediate stage, while low-Hnt egg chambers are the most mature egg chambers.
evidence: This is inferred from the analysis of FC1 expression and nurse cell nuclei counts.

claim: Low-Hnt egg chambers are the most mature egg chambers.
source: Because nurse-cell nuclei are progressively degraded starting around stage-12 by a non-cell-autonomous mechanism to generate fully matured egg chambers, which have no nurse cell nuclei and are dehydrated (Drummond-Barbosa and Spradling, 2004; Timmons et al., 2016), the above analysis demonstrates that high-Hnt egg chambers are at the intermediate stage, while low-Hnt egg chambers are the most mature egg chambers.
evidence: This is inferred from the analysis of FC1 expression and nurse cell nuclei counts.

claim: Both A/P- and high-Hnt egg chambers had no or minimal GFP expression driven by FC2.
source: Consistent with the previous result, both A/P- and high-Hnt egg chambers had no or minimal GFP expression driven by FC2, while low-Hnt egg chambers had highest GFP expression and fewest nurse-cell nuclei (Figure 2F–J).
evidence: This is quantitative data from the study shown in Figure 2I.

claim: Low-Hnt egg chambers had highest GFP expression driven by FC2 and fewest nurse-cell nuclei.
source: Consistent with the previous result, both A/P- and high-Hnt egg chambers had no or minimal GFP expression driven by FC2, while low-Hnt egg chambers had highest GFP expression and fewest nurse-cell nuclei (Figure 2F–J).
evidence: This is quantitative data from the study shown in Figure 2I-J.

claim: Hnt is first upregulated in posterior follicle cells, filled in across the entire egg chamber, and then overall downregulated in follicle cells of fully matured egg chambers.
source: Altogether, these analyses demonstrate that Hnt is first upregulated in posterior follicle cells, filled in across the entire egg chamber, and then overall downregulated in follicle cells of fully matured egg chambers (Figure 2K).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the temporal analysis of Hnt expression shown in Figure 2K.

claim: Stage-14 egg chambers can be categorized into three distinct stages: stage-14A (A/P-Hnt), stage-14B (high-Hnt), and stage-14C (low-Hnt).
source: Therefore, we propose to categorize stage-14 egg chambers into three distinct stages and rename A/P-, high-, and low-Hnt egg chambers as stage-14A, stage-14B, and stage-14C egg chambers, respectively (Figure 2K).
evidence: This is a classification proposed by the authors based on their data.

claim: FC1 was weak to deplete Hnt expression in stage-14A follicle cells.
source: While FC1 started to be expressed in stage-14A follicle cells, it was weak to deplete Hnt expression in stage-14A follicle cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–D), but became progressively more efficient in older follicle cells with two independent hntRNAi lines (Figure 3A–D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E–H); more than 80% of stage-14C egg chambers had no detectable Hnt expression in their follicle cells.
evidence: This is observational data from the study shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–D.

claim: FC1 became progressively more efficient in depleting Hnt in older follicle cells with two independent hntRNAi lines.
source: While FC1 started to be expressed in stage-14A follicle cells, it was weak to deplete Hnt expression in stage-14A follicle cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–D), but became progressively more efficient in older follicle cells with two independent hntRNAi lines (Figure 3A–D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E–H); more than 80% of stage-14C egg chambers had no detectable Hnt expression in their follicle cells.
evidence: This is quantitative data from the study shown in Figure 3A–D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E–H.

claim: More than 80% of stage-14C egg chambers had no detectable Hnt expression in their follicle cells when using FC1 to drive hntRNAi.
source: While FC1 started to be expressed in stage-14A follicle cells, it was weak to deplete Hnt expression in stage-14A follicle cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–D), but became progressively more efficient in older follicle cells with two independent hntRNAi lines (Figure 3A–D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E–H); more than 80% of stage-14C egg chambers had no detectable Hnt expression in their follicle cells.
evidence: This is quantitative data from the study shown in Figure 3D.

claim: FC2 started to be expressed in stage-14B follicle cells and most effectively depleted Hnt expression in stage-14C follicle cells.
source: In contrast, FC2 started to be expressed in stage-14B follicle cells and most effectively depleted Hnt expression in stage-14C follicle cells except with hntRNAi2, which only showed strong reduction in ~43% of egg chambers (Figure 3E–H and Figure 3—figure supplement 1I–P).
evidence: This is observational and quantitative data from the study shown in Figure 3E–H and Figure 3—figure supplement 1I–P.

claim: hntRNAi females laid significantly fewer eggs than control females after mating.
source: hntRNAi females laid significantly fewer eggs than control females after mating (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is quantitative data from the study shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Hnt expression in stage-14 follicle cells is essential for normal egg laying.
source: This phenotype was manifested by using both stage-14 follicle-cell Gal4 drivers and with two independent hntRNAi lines, which demonstrates that Hnt expression in stage-14 follicle cells was essential for normal egg laying.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the egg-laying data using multiple genetic tools.

claim: The decrease in egg-laying number in hntRNAi females was not caused by an oogenesis defect.
source: The decrease in egg-laying number was not caused by an oogenesis defect, as plenty of stage-14 egg chambers were observed before and after egg-laying experiments (Figure 3J and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3J and Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Control females spent 12–14 min to ovulate an egg.
source: Consistent with our previous data, control females spent 12–14 min to ovulate an egg, less than a minute to transport egg through the oviduct, and eight - 10 min to hold an egg in the uterus and oviposit (Figure 3K–L and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is quantitative data from the study shown in Figure 3K–L and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Control females spent less than a minute to transport egg through the oviduct.
source: Consistent with our previous data, control females spent 12–14 min to ovulate an egg, less than a minute to transport egg through the oviduct, and eight - 10 min to hold an egg in the uterus and oviposit (Figure 3K–L and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is quantitative data from the study shown in Figure 3K–L and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Control females spent eight - 10 min to hold an egg in the uterus and oviposit.
source: Consistent with our previous data, control females spent 12–14 min to ovulate an egg, less than a minute to transport egg through the oviduct, and eight - 10 min to hold an egg in the uterus and oviposit (Figure 3K–L and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is quantitative data from the study shown in Figure 3K–L and Supplementary file 1.

claim: hntRNAi females spent more than 25 min to ovulate an egg, which was significantly longer than the control females.
source: In contrast, hntRNAi females spent more than 25 min to ovulate an egg, which was significantly longer than the control females (Figure 3K–L and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is quantitative data from the study shown in Figure 3K–L and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Hnt in stage-14 follicle cells is required for normal ovulation.
source: These data demonstrate that Hnt in stage-14 follicle cells is required for normal ovulation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the egg-laying time analysis.

claim: About 45% stage-14 egg chambers isolated according to FC1 expression from control females ruptured in response to OA stimulation.
source: Consistent with this idea, about 45% stage-14 egg chambers isolated according to FC1 expression from control females ruptured in response to OA stimulation, whereas fewer than 10% of egg chambers from hntRNAi females ruptured in response to OA stimulation (Figure 4A–D).
evidence: This is quantitative data from the study shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Fewer than 10% of egg chambers from hntRNAi females (with FC1) ruptured in response to OA stimulation.
source: Consistent with this idea, about 45% stage-14 egg chambers isolated according to FC1 expression from control females ruptured in response to OA stimulation, whereas fewer than 10% of egg chambers from hntRNAi females ruptured in response to OA stimulation (Figure 4A–D).
evidence: This is quantitative data from the study shown in Figure 4D.

claim: More than 85% stage-14 egg chambers isolated according to FC2 expression from control females ruptured in response to OA stimulation.
source: In addition, more than 85% stage-14 egg chambers isolated according to FC2 expression from control females ruptured in response to OA stimulation (Figure 4E and H), consistent with the fact that FC2 is expressed in more mature egg chambers than FC1 (Figure 2).

evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Hnt directly binds to two adjacent Hnt-binding sequences in the regulatory region of hnt and nervy genes and attenuates their expression.
source: Hnt directly binds to two adjacent Hnt-binding sequences in the regulatory region of hnt and nervy genes and attenuates their expression (Ming et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Hnt-binding motifs are not found in the gene region of Mmp2 and Oamb.
source: Such Hnt-binding motifs are not found in the gene region of Mmp2 and Oamb.
evidence: This is an observation from the study.

claim: Hnt may indirectly regulate Mmp2 expression in posterior follicle cells.
source: Thus, Hnt may indirectly regulate Mmp2 expression in posterior follicle cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the absence of Hnt-binding motifs in the Mmp2 gene region.

claim: Other transcriptional regulators must exist to coordinate with Hnt to restrict Mmp2 expression to posterior follicle cells.
source: In addition, other transcriptional regulators must exist to coordinate with Hnt to restrict Mmp2 expression to posterior follicle cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the spatial restriction of Mmp2 expression.

claim: Hnt has a general role in regulating epithelial integrity in multiple organ systems and developmental stages.
source: Hnt's role in regulating Mmp2 expression and extracellular matrix homeostasis may not be restricted to posterior follicle cells. It has been shown that Hnt has a general role in regulating epithelial integrity in multiple organ systems and developmental stages.
evidence: This is supported by multiple examples cited in the manuscript.

claim: During retinal morphogenesis, hnt mutant photoreceptor cells frequently delaminate from retinal epithelium and are unable to maintain their integrity.
source: During retinal morphogenesis, hnt mutant photoreceptor cells frequently delaminate from retinal epithelium and are unable to maintain their integrity (Pickup et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: In the tracheal system, hnt mutant tracheal epithelium disintegrate to form sacs and vesicles from collapsed dorsal trunk and branches.
source: In the tracheal system, hnt mutant tracheal epithelium disintegrate to form sacs and vesicles from collapsed dorsal trunk and branches (Wilk et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: During oogenesis, Hnt is essential for proper cell adhesion and collective cell migration in stage-9 egg chambers.
source: During oogenesis, Hnt is essential for proper cell adhesion and collective cell migration in stage-9 egg chambers.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Ectopic expression of Hnt in the cluster of border cells leads to dissociation of the border-cell cluster.
source: Ectopic expression of Hnt in the cluster of border cells leads to dissociation of the border-cell cluster (Melani et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Genetic modifier screens identify basement-membrane components Vkg and Laminin as Hnt's genetic interactors.
source: In addition, genetic modifier screens identify basement-membrane components Vkg and Laminin as Hnt's genetic interactors (Wilk et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Hnt plays general roles in regulating epithelial integrity and extracellular matrix homeostasis in multiple organ systems.
source: All of these studies suggest that Hnt plays general roles in regulating epithelial integrity and extracellular matrix homeostasis in multiple organ systems.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple previous studies.

claim: Drosophila Hnt and mammalian RREB-1 are functionally conserved in many aspects.
source: Drosophila Hnt and mammalian RREB-1 are functionally conserved in many aspects.
evidence: This is supported by multiple examples in the manuscript.

claim: Both Drosophila Hnt and mammalian RREB-1 are required for proper cell migration.
source: Both Drosophila Hnt and mammalian RREB-1 are required for proper cell migration (Melani et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Human RREB-1 binds to similar DNA sequences in Drosophila salivary gland polytene chromosomes as Hnt.
source: Human RREB-1 binds to similar DNA sequences in Drosophila salivary gland polytene chromosomes as Hnt and rescues the germ band retraction phenotype in hnt mutant embryos (Ming et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Human RREB-1 rescues the germ band retraction phenotype in hnt mutant embryos.
source: Human RREB-1 binds to similar DNA sequences in Drosophila salivary gland polytene chromosomes as Hnt and rescues the germ band retraction phenotype in hnt mutant embryos (Ming et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: The role of RREB-1 in mammalian ovulation has not been studied so far.
source: The role of RREB-1 in mammalian ovulation has not been studied so far, however, RREB-1 is detected in granulosa cells in mouse ovaries by microarray analysis (Fan et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: RREB-1 is detected in granulosa cells in mouse ovaries by microarray analysis.
source: The role of RREB-1 in mammalian ovulation has not been studied so far, however, RREB-1 is detected in granulosa cells in mouse ovaries by microarray analysis (Fan et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Mammalian RREB-1 functions downstream of the Ras-MAPK signaling pathway in multiple occasions.
source: In addition, mammalian RREB-1 functions downstream of the Ras-MAPK signaling pathway in multiple occasions (Kent et al., 2010; 2013; Mukhopadhyay et al., 2007; Thiagalingam et al., 1996; Zhang et al., 2003), and the Ras-MAPK signaling pathway is involved in mammalian ovulation (Fan et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: The Ras-MAPK signaling pathway is involved in mammalian ovulation.
source: In addition, mammalian RREB-1 functions downstream of the Ras-MAPK signaling pathway in multiple occasions (Kent et al., 2010; 2013; Mukhopadhyay et al., 2007; Thiagalingam et al., 1996; Zhang et al., 2003), and the Ras-MAPK signaling pathway is involved in mammalian ovulation (Fan et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: It is possible that RREB-1 may function in granulosa cells to regulate Mmp expression and ovulation downstream of Ras-MAPK pathway in mammals.
source: It is possible that RREB-1 may function in granulosa cells to regulate Mmp expression and ovulation downstream of Ras-MAPK pathway in mammals.
evidence: This is speculated based on the conservation between Hnt and RREB-1 and the involvement of Ras-MAPK in mammalian ovulation.
